opening_message:
Ticket 1: Matthew Mejia (employee ID E034) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E034.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Matthew Mejia (E034) is a full-time Analyst. Full-time employees may have up to write access, and admin requires owning the role's system (Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Analyst). Requested write to Payroll is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Matthew Mejia (E034) is a contractor with basic security training (note: this differs from HR's note of full-time). Contractors max is read with basic training (write requires advanced training, never admin). Requested write to Payroll exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: There is a factual conflict between the two notes for E034: HR records Matthew Mejia as a full-time Analyst (full-time max is write for Payroll since Analyst doesn't own Payroll), while Security records him as a contractor with basic security training (contractor max is read without advanced training). Because the employment record is disputed and write access would exceed the contractor/basic limit, I apply the more restrictive classification. Requested write exceeds the contractor max of read, so grant read.
